docs.purpose: Lets an admin view every tunable business setting the pricing and forecasting engine uses — cost rates, trade timing windows, scope allocation percentages — and save edits to them, which the pipeline picks up on its next run.
docs.data_story: It reads 4 tables — `logic_variables`, `trade_configurations`, `trade_sqft_rates` and `scope_intensity_matrix` and writes `logic_variables`, `trade_configurations`, `trade_sqft_rates` and `scope_intensity_matrix`. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 4 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 2 places: `src/features/admin-controls/api/useGetConfigs.ts`, `src/features/admin-controls/api/useUpdateConfigs.ts`. It mutates admin state and writes **no `admin_audit_log` row** — one of the nine measured gaps Phase 0 closes.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

Every table and column declared in lineage.reads[]/writes[] must exist in src/lib/db/generated/schema.ts (drizzle-kit introspect of the live database); the registry generator checks this both directions.
